briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-013
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- office roof: (123, 68), roof
- water tower top: (-105, -145), roof
- pump house: (75, 21), indoor
- workshop: (-20, 125), indoor
- workcell West: (46, -72), indoor
- parking lot: (-10, -71), outdoor
- loading dock: (-120, -82), outdoor
- site B: (27, -49), outdoor

Robots:
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 6.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1440 s, including the return to its start.
- A1 (fixed_arm): installed at workcell West and cannot move; it can only work on tasks located at workcell West. Equipment: robotic arm. Mains-powered (no endurance limit).
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 7 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1260 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 10 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2820 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 8 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3360 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Photograph workshop for the condition report. Location: workshop. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 240 s.
- T2: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 180 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T3: Tighten the valve at loading dock. Location: loading dock. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 720 s.
- T4: Photograph loading dock for the condition report. Location: loading dock. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 180 s.
- T5: Run a thermal scan of site B. Location: site B. Duration: 120 s. Needs: thermal camera. Deadline: finished by t = 420 s.
- T6: Inspect water tower top with a camera. Location: water tower top. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T7: Run a thermal scan of water tower top. Location: water tower top. Duration: 210 s. Needs: thermal camera. Deadline: finished by t = 600 s.
- T8: Deliver the first-aid kit (4 kg) to workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 4 kg).
- T9: Photograph loading dock for the condition report. Location: loading dock. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera.
- T10: Replace the filter cartridge at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 180 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T8 is finished.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Keep at least 1 quadcopter on standby: it must not be given any task.
6. Every task must be finished by t = 1200 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Here's what we need from the robots today.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: office roof (123, 68, a rooftop); water tower top (-105, -145, a rooftop); pump house (75, 21, indoors); workshop (-20, 125, indoors); workcell West (46, -72, indoors); parking lot (-10, -71, outside); loading dock (-120, -82, outside); site B (27, -49, outside).

The fleet: D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 6.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 24 minutes including the flight home. A1 is a robot arm bolted down in workcell West; it can't move but can work on jobs inside workcell West, and it runs on mains power. D2, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera and a thermal camera, cruises at 7 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 21 minutes of flight time, return trip included. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 10 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 47 minutes including getting back. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 8 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 56 minutes including getting back.

Jobs:
(T1) We need pictures of workshop for the report - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 4 minutes.
(T2) The valve at workcell West needs tightening - that takes 3 minutes on site.
(T3) The valve at loading dock needs tightening - that takes 4 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 12 minutes.
(T4) Document loading dock with pictures - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 3 minutes.
(T5) Look for overheating equipment around site B - that takes 2 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 7 minutes.
(T6) Do a visual check of water tower top - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T7) Look for overheating equipment around water tower top - that takes 3.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 10 minutes.
(T8) Workcell West needs the first-aid kit, which weighs 4 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T9) Grab photos of loading dock for the condition report - that takes 2 minutes on site.
(T10) Change the filter at workcell West - that takes 3 minutes on site but only once the first-aid kit (T8) has arrived.

Keep one quadcopter on standby; don't give it any jobs. Everything has to be wrapped up within 20 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
